To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Treg cells express Foxo1, which is required for their function; 2) Treg cells display low levels of Akt activation and high levels of Foxo1 activity; 3) Foxo1 is required for the expression of the Ifng gene; 4) Treg cell-specific deletion of Fox1 results in a fatal inflammatory disorder; 5) Foxo1 binds to ∼300 genes that include Ifng, but not Foxp3.

Foxo1, a transcription factor that regulates metabolism in other cells, controls a novel transcriptional program essential for the function of Treg cells, which are specialized immune cells that maintain immune homeostasiss and prevent autoimmune disorders.
Foxo1, a member of a conserved family of transcription factors, is a novel regulator of Treg-cell function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control regulatory T (Treg)-cell homeostasis and suppressive functions.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate Treg cell function and homeostasis.
the role of the transcription factor Foxo1 in the development and function of regulatory T-cells (Treg cells).
